title: Design System: Eagle’s Dominion Synergy Assembly

display.purpose: Manrope scene headings with compressed leading and assertive weight.

editorial.purpose: Newsreader for Scripture, declarations, citations, and selected reflective phrases.

title.purpose: Manrope titles inside photographic chapters and intermediate story beats.

body.purpose: Manrope explanatory prose and practical guidance.

label.purpose: Compact service metadata, actions, navigation, and citations.

hero-display.purpose: Outfit display typography scoped only to the immutable opening hero.

motion.name: ease-out-ui

motion.name: ease-in-out-ui

motion.name: state-color

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Compact active compression and hover lift on actions.

motion.name: chapter-image
motion.purpose: Fine-pointer image scale response inside experience chapters.

motion.name: scripture-reveal

narrative.overview:
The Editorial Sanctuary combines the gravity of a midnight worship space with the clarity of a premium editorial publication. Distinct scenes shift between navy-black atmosphere, ivory and paper utility, amber warmth, and vivid human photography, so the experience feels cinematic without obscuring service information or the next action.

The system is premium through restraint: flat tonal layers, near-square compositions, disciplined type, compact controls, and carefully placed Scripture. Manrope carries navigation, display, body, and utility work; Newsreader introduces a spiritual editorial cadence; Outfit belongs only to the approved opening hero. Real EDSA people and places provide emotion and proof rather than generic church imagery.

Motion creates continuity, never meaning. The opening sequence may be immersive and the preaching stage may use restrained depth on capable desktop devices, while every other state remains complete, legible, and composed without animation.
keyCharacteristics: Distinct editorial scenes joined by a controlled midnight, navy, paper, ivory, and amber palette.
Real human photography in squared or near-square crops, with scrims used only for legibility.
Dense display typography balanced by compact, practical action hierarchy.
Flat tonal layering and deliberate overlap instead of decorative shadow stacks.
Restrained, interruptible motion with static mobile, coarse-pointer, and reduced-motion compositions.

rules.name: The Scene Contrast Rule
rules.body: Adjacent scenes must change tone, composition, or photographic density clearly enough to feel intentional while remaining part of the same navy-led world.

rules.name: The Amber Restraint Rule
rules.body: Amber is a moment of warmth or witness, not the default button, body-text, or navigation color.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Manrope owns the interface and post-hero hierarchy, Newsreader is reserved for Scripture and selected editorial phrases, and Outfit appears only inside the approved hero.

rules.name: The Editorial Phrase Rule
rules.body: Newsreader should punctuate a Manrope-led composition; it must not become the default body or navigation face.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest on one plane; use tonal contrast, overlap, or a one-pixel divider before reaching for a shadow.

rules.name: The Square Form Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce rounded cards, pills, or capsule actions into this system; hierarchy comes from proportion, contrast, and placement.

rules.name: The Compact Action Rule
rules.body: One filled action leads; secondary actions remain outlined or text-led and must not compete with it in weight.

dos: **Do** build pages as a sequence of visibly distinct scenes held together by the same type roles and navy-led palette.
**Do** use real EDSA people, worship, teaching, children, and place photography in intentional square or near-square crops.
**Do** keep one filled action visually primary and make service information immediately scannable.
**Do** preserve complete static compositions for mobile, coarse pointers, loading failure, and reduced motion.
**Do** use Manrope for practical clarity and reserve Newsreader for Scripture or a selected editorial phrase.
donts: **Don't** introduce rounded cards, pill buttons, soft dashboard panels, or decorative shadow stacks.
**Don't** let Outfit escape the approved hero or let Newsreader become the default interface face.
**Don't** reuse a photograph within the same narrative surface or substitute generic stock-spiritual imagery for real human evidence.
**Don't** make meaning, service information, or an action depend on animation, hover, or pointer depth.
**Don't** flood the interface with amber; its rarity gives it warmth and authority.
